questions.question: Write a short note on the contributions of Siegfried Sassoon to war poetry. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Siegfried Sassoon-His collection, Counter-Attack exposes the visceral horror, strategic
  • incompetence and futility of trench warfare through direct, unflinching language- savagely
  • condemns the older generation of officers who sent young men to die – he issued a public
  • protest in 1917, declaring the war a “senseless slaughter.” Sassoon’s voice of outrage and
  • moral clarity gave war poetry a new, searing honesty—a refusal to glorify and a demand for
  • accountability. (CO1)

questions.question: Explain Ferdinand de Saussure’s view of language as a structured system of signs. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• The signifier- the sound-image or written form of a word-the signified: the mental
  • concept or meaning it evokes -the relationship between the signifier and the signified is
  • arbitrary-Meaning, is not inherent but arises from difference within the language system.
  • Language is a network of contrasting relations. Saussure also made a key distinction between:
  • Langue: The underlying, shared system of a language—its grammar,rules and vocabulary—
  • that exists collectively among speakers-Parole-the individual act of speaking or writing.
  • (CO1)

questions.question: Explain the contribution of modern non-fiction writers to British cultural and intellectual thought in the early twentieth century. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• An age of rapid industrialisation, scientific advancement, urban expansion and shifting
  • moral values- novelists sought new narrative techniques -reflect a fragmented, uncertain
  • modern reality-Traditional plots, chronological narratives and objective description were
  • frequently replaced by experimental forms, multiple perspectives and symbolic or
  • impressionistic styles- the stream-of-consciousness technique -Writers such as James Joyce,
  • Virginia Woolf and D. H. Lawrence transformed the possibilities of fiction by probing themes
  • of identity, sexuality, class conflict, personal freedom and the search for meaning in an
  • unstable world. Aldous Huxley, George Orwell and Graham Greene - extended the scope of
  • modern fiction by examining the ethical, political and social crises of the twentieth century
  • through dystopian visions, political allegory and morally complex narratives. (CO2)
